Q: What is the correct way of code comments in JavaScript? A:

Using // is better than /* */ because then you can use the latter to take out an entire block containing other comments. However, if you want to use an automatic documentation generation tool, you must use comments similar to javaDoc style.

This is an example that would work with YUIDoc (best one):

/**
* This is a description
* @namespace My.Namespace
* @method myMethodName
* @param {String} some string
* @param {Object} some object
* @return {bool} some bool
*/

Q: Cleaning/deleting /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io A:

A short and blithe answer: don't worry about /run/k3s.

The directories /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/*/rootfsare just mount points for overlayfs. Each presents actual layers located under /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd. If you're "running out of space" on /run/k3s, your real issue is (should be) with the volume hosting the actual layers.

# rootfs size matches volume /var/lib/rancher
df -m | grep "9358d52eb4a76\|var/lib/rancher"
/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-rancher--storage       61420 15258     46163  25% /var/lib/rancher
overlay                                       61420 15258     46163  25% /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/9358d52eb4a764df635995e83b5a03e79545192f75b85b1a8942e029ce48b62d/rootfs 

# the reason is its constituent layers are in /var/lib/rancher
mount | grep 9358d52eb4a76
overlay on /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/9358d52eb4a764df635995e83b5a03e79545192f75b85b1a8942e029ce48b62d/rootfs type overlay (rw,relatime,lowerdir=/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136313/fs,upperdir=/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136418/fs,workdir=/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136418/work,uuid=on,nouserxattr)

# write 2GiB to /tmp in the container
kubectl exec -it ubuntu -- dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/bigfile bs=2G count=1

# the mountpoint shows the total size
du -sh /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/9358d52eb4a764df635995e83b5a03e79545192f75b85b1a8942e029ce48b62d/rootfs
2.1G    /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/9358d52eb4a764df635995e83b5a03e79545192f75b85b1a8942e029ce48b62d/rootfs

# sizes of the constituent layers
du -sh /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136313/fs
82M /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136313/fs
root@srv01:~# du -sh /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136418/fs
2.0G    /var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/containerd/io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs/snapshots/136418/fs

# the volume mounted at /var/lib/rancher has grown in size
df -m | grep "9358d52eb4a76\|var/lib/rancher"
/dev/mapper/ubuntu--vg-rancher--storage       61420 17324     44097  29% /var/lib/rancher
overlay                                       61420 17324     44097  29% /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/9358d52eb4a764df635995e83b5a03e79545192f75b85b1a8942e029ce48b62d/rootfs

Orphan directories with stale data

There's a directory in /run/k3s for each unique container and pod, as you've found out. The total of containers and pods should match the directory count:

crictl ps -o json|jq -r '.containers[]|"\(.id)\n\(.podSandboxId)"'|sort|uniq|wc -l
47

ls /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io/|wc -l
47

If the numbers don't match, you may have consulted a certain document that describes /run/k3s as "runtime data" and you created a volume for it. Do not do this. /runis a tmpfs volume that gets deleted every shutdown.

df -m /run
Filesystem     1M-blocks  Used Available Use% Mounted on
tmpfs               3198     6      3193   1% /run

How to check the total rootfs size per container

You only see ephemeral usage with crictl stats. If you just want to see how much disk space each container consumes (image plus ephemeral, not PVs):

cd /run/k3s/containerd/io.containerd.runtime.v2.task/k8s.io
crictl ps -o json \
  | jq -r '.containers[] | [.metadata.name, .labels["io.kubernetes.pod.namespace"], .id, .podSandboxId] | @tsv' \
  | while read NAME NS CONTAINERID PODID
    do echo $NS/$NAME
      du -sh $CONTAINERID
    done
ingress-nginx/controller
248M    899ac0c7cd0d8951f5b130bab32c4a75a5bb168535e8f884fe9e3bb120ede12f
cert-manager/cert-manager-controller
81M 66f5b4e1f6d15f94683c71abfd10b6f2721b6ac45d72617f9784cc24fb828486

Q: How can I match comma-separated values to further plot them in Power BI? A:

Conduct the transformation in PowerQuery,

let
    Source = Table.FromRows(Json.Document(Binary.Decompress(Binary.FromText("i45WSjZU0lHKTAGRRkBcZKhTBKJTDHVSjJRideAKQILGIAXGOkUmOkWmIDXGOikmOimmSrGxAA==", BinaryEncoding.Base64), Compression.Deflate)), let _t = ((type nullable text) meta [Serialized.Text = true]) in type table [Circle = _t, id = _t, count = _t, remark = _t, date = _t]),
    Cols = {"remark","date"},
    #"Combined Cols" = Table.CombineColumns(Source, Cols, each Table.FromColumns(List.Transform(_, each Text.Split(_, ",")), Cols), "cmb"),
    #"Expanded cmb" = Table.ExpandTableColumn(#"Combined Cols", "cmb", Cols)
in
    #"Expanded cmb"

Q: Why private field handling does not work in an expected way in JavaScript? A:

The error message "Cannot read private member #saveSuspend from an object whose class did not declare it" is slightly confusing. More accurate in this case would be "from an object where it is not (yet) initialised".

Private fields, and fields in general, are created on the instance (and initialised with the value defined in the class body) when the super() constructor returns. If that constructor is calling an overridden method (configure) before the initialisation is done, it will not be able to access the non-existing field. With private fields, it just throws an exception because the field doesn't exist, instead of returning undefined like a normal property.

The only solution is to never call an overrideable method from a constructor. This is true in any language. In your case, just get rid of the configure method altogether, it does not thing.
